steps.note: The permeate is seeded, then cooled slowly, about 3 °C/h from 60 to 30 °C and about 1.5 °C/h to 15 °C, so the lactose comes out as crystals over 0.2 mm, which separate best.

lactose.text: Lactose is much less soluble when cold, so a concentrated permeate is cooled slowly and the lactose crystallises out (as alpha-lactose monohydrate). The crystals are spun off, washed and dried; the mother liquor keeps the minerals and the rest of the sugar.
